<!-- goose-evidence:issue-6134:workflow-proof -->
🤖 **Automated evidence (Wails Goose maintainer agent): reproduction + fix validation**

**Environment** (native isolated guest; *not* the reporter's host)
- Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-38-generic aarch64, `go1.27.1 linux/arm64`.
- Genuinely **split mounts**: staging on tmpfs `/dev/shm` (**dev=0x1c**) vs the install target on ext4 `/home/$USER` (**dev=0xfd02**). A raw `rename(2)` across them returns `EXDEV`/errno 18, so the fallback is exercised against a **real** cross-device move, not an injected synthetic error.

**Reproduction — pre-fix base `aa1c3c67bae79d9f72ab0899bcdda1132545004d`**
- A real `replaceTarget(target, newPath)` across the two mounts returned `invalid cross-device link`.
- End state: target `exists=false`, `content=""`, `mode=0` — the working binary was removed and nothing was put back, matching the report's "only `Application.bak` remained".

**Fix validation — PR #6135 head `12178f4bb527faa93a826d193974400081d36f31`**
- Same real cross-device layout: the swap succeeded, target `content=="NEW-BINARY"`, mode **0755** preserved, staged source consumed, and no `.wails-update-*` staging leftover.

**Real split-filesystem regression test** (see the PR #6135 comment for the file)
- New `TestRealEXDEV_*` coverage drives `replaceTarget`/`runHelperSwap` across two genuinely different mounts (asserting a real `os.Rename` → `EXDEV` first), plus a copy-failure failure-safety case. Passes on this host (gofmt/vet clean). This is the real-split-mount coverage the "Suggested Fix" asks for.

**Limitations**
- Unit-level reproduction/validation of `pkg/updater` against real filesystems; a full signed-release app-update flow (build → provider → in-app restart) was **not** run here, and other OSes are out of scope for this check. Not full release acceptance.

The fix already exists in community PR #6135 (all required checks green, awaiting review). No duplicate fix branch is being opened.


---

<!-- goose-full-suite-race -->
**Additional native check — full updater suite with race detector (repaired fixture)**

After the first trimmed-fixture attempt failed on an unrelated missing guard file, I rebuilt the fixture to include the exact PR-head TypeScript guard `internal/runtime/desktop/@wailsio/runtime/src/updater.ts` (sha256 `3b9dd93044e21a9a402406f7c745c7205fb4e09d4a206df8d56808d205e971c4`) — no test was removed or skipped. On the same Ubuntu 26.04.1 guest (archive sha256 `756ae7df1ed9e532d1dcc2b75df6c2b0f9050e931d2b2b1b8938978de1ea8342`, regression-test file sha256 `23cd632f61270655dd0cc397453a747c929858830b3744ec7d6849f8d12cfbf8`):

- `gofmt -l pkg/updater/helper_unix_realexdev_test.go` → clean (exit 0)
- `go vet ./pkg/updater/...` → exit 0
- `go test -race -count=1 ./pkg/updater/...` → **exit 0**; all packages `ok` (`pkg/updater` 27.9s, `internal/semver`, `providers/{appcast,endpoint,github,keygen}`).

Still in scope limits: unit-level `pkg/updater` validation against real filesystems; no end-to-end signed-release flow and other OSes are out of scope. Not full release acceptance.
